Part 2 · Stage by stage

What goes in, and where does the simulator feed it?

Part 2 · the plan

Facts in, then hypotheses

The OTS supplies the facts; the workbook keeps them apart from opinions.

  1. Where the OTS feeds each stagerun, snapshot, event log, field calls
  2. The evidence listfact, inference or opinion, with a time
  3. The data you pullruns as tables and plots

Stages and the OTS · interactive

Where does the simulator feed each stage?

The OTS answers what happened; the workbook asks why, in a fixed order.

TE-1 evidence · interactive

Fourteen items, each with a source

Thirteen facts and one opinion: the opinion is kept, labelled, and never used as proof.

OTS data · interactive

A run becomes a table and a plot

Run

Tag

One sample per minute, pulled live in the tab or imported as CSV into the standalone copy.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Each stage has its OTS source: run, snapshot, log or call.
  • Evidence is labelled fact, inference or opinion, with a time.
  • Runs come in as tables, then plots and figures.

Part 3 · From decision to hand-in

How does a finished workbook close?

Part 3 · the plan

Decide, count the cost, hand in

TE-1 is the worked case: open it from Worked examples and follow along.

  1. The decision matrixweights × scores for the solution options
  2. The cost ledgerwhat the upset and the tests cost
  3. Report, slides and savewhat the group hands in

Stage 5 · interactive

Which option wins, and how robust is it?

\(W_i = \sum_j w_j\,s_{ij}\) · weight \(w_j\) of criterion \(j\) (sums to 1) × score \(s_{ij}\) of option \(i\), 1–5

Restoring the preheat wins unless feasibility and time weigh three times more than cost.

Stages 4–6 · interactive

What did TE-1 cost?

USD in the ledger

The tests cost about 200 USD; the lost margin and off-spec product cost over 30,000.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Options are ranked by weighted score \(W_i\); check the weights.
  • The ledger shows the upset costs more than the tests.
  • Hand in the report, the slides and the .woods.json.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Open the workbook in the tab to pull live data.

2

Fill the ★ sub-steps first, in stage order.

3

Label every item fact, inference or opinion.

4

Test the decision against other weights.

5

Save the .woods.json before you close.
